title: The first chip
text: In 1971, Intel put a whole computer on one chip. The 4004 had about two thousand three hundred transistors.

title: Eight bits
text: In 1974, the 8080 gave computers eight bits of power, fast enough for early personal machines.

title: The x86 begins
text: In 1978, Intel launched the 8086, the chip that started the x86 line still used in PCs today.

title: Thirty two bits
text: In 1985, the 386 brought thirty two bits to personal computers, letting them run more software.

title: Pentium
text: In 1993, Intel introduced the Pentium, a faster chip for a new era of computing.

title: Many cores
text: By 2005, chips got more than one core, so a computer could do several things at once.

title: Phones get powerful
text: In the twenty tens, phone chips caught up to laptop chips, and a pocket computer could edit video.

title: What is coming?
text: Now chips train neural networks, and the next step is silicon built for artificial intelligence. Which chip would you pick? Tell me in the comments.
